title: Tesla + SpaceX? The deal terms matter more than the headline

sources.note: Special committee exploring deeper relationship with SpaceX including possible business combination; no assurance of consummation.

claims.text: Tesla disclosed a special committee exploring a deeper relationship with SpaceX, including a possible business combination.
The filing says there is no assurance that a transaction will be consummated.
Illustration only: 10 shares out of 100 is 10%; if total shares increase to 125 while those 10 are retained, the stake is 8%.
A lower ownership percentage alone does not establish a lower investment value; what is acquired and the price paid matter.

scenes.title: Tesla + SpaceX? Start with the terms.
scenes.narration: A possible combination sounds huge. But the useful question is what shareholders would get, and what they would give up.

scenes.title: A committee. No guaranteed deal.
scenes.narration: Tesla disclosed a committee exploring a deeper relationship with SpaceX, including a possible business combination. Its filing says a transaction is not assured.

scenes.title: Your share count can stay the same.
scenes.narration: Imagine you own ten of a company's hundred shares. If it issues twenty-five more, your ownership falls from ten percent to eight percent.

scenes.title: A smaller slice of what?
scenes.narration: That does not automatically make you poorer. The company may gain valuable assets. The question is whether what it receives justifies what it pays.
labels: Ownership percentage is not investment value

scenes.title: Three questions beat one big headline.
scenes.narration: What is the price? How would ownership change? And who must approve it? Those answers matter more than assuming a merger will happen.

scenes.title: Separate the announcement from the outcome.
scenes.narration: This is an explanation of deal mechanics, not a forecast. Our share-count example is illustrative, not a proposed Tesla or SpaceX exchange ratio.
